packageRules.description: Everything non-major goes in one PR and merges itself. These are small, frequent and reversible by putting the old tag back.

Majors get their own PR and are never merged automatically. A database major cannot be done by swapping the tag -- PostgreSQL refuses to start on a data directory written by another major, so the data has to be dumped and restored first. Grouping majors with patches (separateMajorMinor: false) once put postgres 17 -> 18 in the same automerged PR as an nginx patch. Labelled needs-review so the repository's Claude review workflow can opt these in: reviewing a PR that merges itself is wasted, reviewing one that waits for a human is not.

Helm charts are never merged automatically, whatever the update type. A chart's version says nothing about how much of the deployment changes: erpnext went 8.0.15 -> 8.0.78, a "patch", and swapped its cache and queue from Dragonfly to Valkey, silently voiding the memory limits that were set in values (danything/gitops#25). Separating majors does not catch that. They get their own group so that holding them back does not also hold back the all-dependencies PR. Labelled needs-review so the repository's Claude review workflow can opt these in: reviewing a PR that merges itself is wasted, reviewing one that waits for a human is not.

Libraries publish peerDependencies as the range they work with. Bumping it to the latest version would force every consumer to upgrade, so peers are widened instead (^5.0.0 -> ^5.0.0 || ^6.0.0) and everything else is bumped. Bumping (rather than updating only the lockfile) is the default because Renovate cannot do lockfile-only updates on bun.lock: in-range security fixes were being closed without being applied.

svelte-check needs TypeScript 6 and 7 installed side by side, and reads the 7 half through the @typescript/native alias. Bumping the typescript entry to 7 leaves no 6 to pair with, which stops `bun run check` from starting at all. Hold it back until svelte-check drops the dual requirement. This was repeated in ashi, blog, lgtm, xool, yosegaki, mogiri and svelte-slider, so it lives here now; repositories that need a stricter cap (denpa: <6) keep their own rule, which wins because it comes later.

Wait an hour after a GitHub release is published before proposing it. A release's tag appears first and its assets are uploaded minutes later; Renovate saw Infisical/cli v0.43.141 in that gap, and the PR's image build (which downloads the asset and checks it against the release's checksum file) failed with a 404 (danything/gitops#327, 2026-10-09: CI at 18:37 UTC, assets uploaded 18:45). An hour is enough for the uploads and short enough not to delay anything noticeably.
